---
title: "Universal REML-BLUP for SNP and Microhaplotype Genomic Prediction"
---

## Universal REML-BLUP for SNP and Microhaplotype Genomic Prediction {.unnumbered}


### Description

BLUP-based model for genomic prediction using SNP or multi-allelic
markers. Estimates variance components via REML and predicts genomic
estimated breeding values (GEBV) via BLUP. Supports SNP additive,
SNP dominance, and multi-allelic additive relationship matrices, for both
continuous and binary traits. For GWAS-assisted prediction, see
<code>run_gwas</code> and <code>gwablup</code>.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>masreml(
  y,
  X = NULL,
  markers = NULL,
  G = NULL,
  method = "auto",
  solver = "auto",
  max_iter = 100L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  n_threads = NULL,
  trait = "continuous",
  link = "logit",
  verbose = TRUE,
  save_rds = FALSE,
  save_path = NULL
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
numeric vector of phenotypes (length n). Named vector
recommended for ID alignment. For binary trait, must contain
only 0 and 1.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
fixed effects design matrix (n x c). If NULL, intercept
only is used.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="markers">markers</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker inputs (optional):


<ul>
<li> <code>snp_add</code>: matrix (n x m), raw genotype 0/1/2

</li>
<li> <code>snp_dom</code>: matrix (n x m), raw genotype 0/1/2

</li>
<li> <code>mh_add</code>: list of data.frames, one per chromosome.
First column = individual ID, remaining columns = paired
haplotype allele codes per block (strand1, strand2, strand1, ...)

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="G">G</code></td>
<td>
list of pre-built relationship matrices (optional):


<ul>
<li> <code>snp_add</code>: numeric matrix (n x n), SNP additive G

</li>
<li> <code>snp_dom</code>: numeric matrix (n x n), SNP dominance D

</li>
<li> <code>mh_add</code>: numeric matrix (n x n), multi-allelic additive Agh

</li>
<li> <code>pedigree</code>: numeric matrix (n x n), pedigree A

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="method">method</code></td>
<td>
character, REML algorithm for variance component estimation:


<ul>
<li> <code>"auto"</code> (default): AI-REML for continuous,
HE regression for binary

</li>
<li> <code>"HE"</code>: Haseman-Elston regression (fast, one-step)

</li>
<li> <code>"AI"</code>: Average Information REML (accurate, iterative)

</li>
<li> <code>"EM"</code>: Expectation-Maximization REML (stable, slower)

</li>
<li> <code>"HI"</code>: HE-initialized AI-REML

</li></ul>

For binary trait, <code>"HE"</code> is recommended for speed.
Any method can be used but <code>"AI"</code> may be slow on working response.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="solver">solver</code></td>
<td>
character, EBV solver:


<ul>
<li> <code>"auto"</code> (default): Cholesky for n &lt; 10,000, PCG otherwise

</li>
<li> <code>"cholesky"</code>: direct Cholesky factorization

</li>
<li> <code>"pcg"</code>: preconditioned conjugate gradient (large n)

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="max_iter">max_iter</code></td>
<td>
integer, maximum REML iterations (default 100)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="tol">tol</code></td>
<td>
numeric, convergence tolerance (default 1e-6)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="n_threads">n_threads</code></td>
<td>
integer, number of threads (default: all physical cores)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="trait">trait</code></td>
<td>
character, trait distribution:


<ul>
<li> <code>"continuous"</code> (default): Gaussian REML-BLUP

</li>
<li> <code>"binary"</code>: 0/1 phenotype, single-step Laplace
approximation on liability scale

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="link">link</code></td>
<td>
character, link function for binary trait:


<ul>
<li> <code>"logit"</code> (default): logistic link, sigma2_e = pi^2/3

</li>
<li> <code>"probit"</code>: probit link, sigma2_e = 1

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="verbose">verbose</code></td>
<td>
logical, if <code>TRUE</code> (default) prints a brief
post-fit summary banner (algorithm, runtime, convergence, variance
components, h2, GEBV summary) when <code>masreml()</code> returns. The
existing progress messages (<code>"Building..."</code>, <code>"Running
  REML..."</code>, <code>"Solving EBV..."</code>) are unaffected by this flag.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="save_rds">save_rds</code></td>
<td>
logical, if <code>TRUE</code> the fit is also written to
disk as an RDS file. Default <code>FALSE</code> <em>(differs from
<code>masbayes::run_bayesr()</code>)</em> because <code>masreml()</code> is often
called inside <code>cv_masreml</code> loops where auto-saving
would clobber per-fold output. Set to <code>TRUE</code> for one-off
full-data fits you want to persist.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="save_path">save_path</code></td>
<td>
optional explicit RDS path. If <code>NULL</code> (default),
defaults to <code>"results_masreml.Rds"</code> in the current working
directory. Ignored unless <code>save_rds = TRUE</code>.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<strong>Statistical model.</strong>
The general mixed linear model is:

<p style="text-align: center;">$y = Xb + \sum_{k} Z_k u_k + e$


with independent random genetic effects
$u_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,G_k \sigma_{g_k}^2)$ and residuals
$e \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,I \sigma_e^2)$, where $G_k$ is the
genomic relationship matrix for component $k$
(<code>snp_add</code>, <code>snp_dom</code>, <code>mh_add</code>, or <code>pedigree</code>).
For a single additive microhaplotype component this reduces to:

<p style="text-align: center;">$y = Xb + Z a_h + e, \quad a_h \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,A_{gh}\,\sigma_{a_h}^2)$


where $A_{gh} = W_{ah} W_{ah}^\top / k_{ah}$ and
$k_{ah} = \mathrm{tr}(W_{ah} W_{ah}^\top) / n$
(Da, 2015; see <code>build_G_mh</code>).
Variance components are estimated by REML; GEBVs are obtained by BLUP.

<strong>Auto-summary.</strong> On completion, <code>masreml()</code> prints a brief
banner mirroring <code>masbayes::run_bayesr()</code>/
<code>masbayes::run_bayesa()</code>. Set <code>verbose = FALSE</code> to suppress.
The full <code>summary.masreml</code> method is unchanged and is
still the canonical detailed report.

<strong>Runtime field.</strong> The returned object now contains a
<code>runtime</code> field (elapsed seconds for REML + BLUP), populated
even when <code>verbose = FALSE</code>.



### Value

Object of class <code>"masreml"</code> with elements:


<ul>
<li> <code>gebv</code>: named list of GEBV vectors per component

</li>
<li> <code>total_gebv</code>: total GEBV (sum across components)

</li>
<li> <code>fixed_effects</code>: fixed effect estimates

</li>
<li> <code>varcomp</code>: list with <code>sigma2</code> and <code>h2</code>

</li>
<li> <code>loglik</code>: restricted log-likelihood

</li>
<li> <code>algorithm</code>: REML algorithm used

</li>
<li> <code>solver</code>: EBV solver used

</li>
<li> <code>converged</code>: logical, convergence status

</li>
<li> <code>n_iter</code>: number of REML iterations

</li>
<li> <code>n</code>: number of individuals

</li>
<li> <code>runtime</code>: elapsed seconds for REML + BLUP

</li>
<li> <code>rds_path</code>: path of saved RDS file, or <code>NULL</code>
when <code>save_rds = FALSE</code>

</li>
<li> <code>training_metrics</code>: list of training-set fit metrics.
Continuous: <code>R2</code>, <code>RMSE</code>, <code>accuracy</code> (Pearson
<em>r</em>), <code>bias</code> (slope of $y \sim \hat{y}$). Binary:
same fields plus <code>AUC</code>, computed on the observed
(probability) scale (<code>y_01</code> vs <code>mu_hat</code>) so that
<code>bias</code> is the <em>calibration slope</em> (1.0 = perfectly
calibrated) and <code>RMSE\^2</code> approximates the Brier score.
<code>AUC</code> is rank-invariant under inverse-link transformation.

</li>
<li> <code>call</code>: matched call

</li></ul>

For binary trait (<code>trait = "binary"</code>), additional
<code>binary</code> slot contains:


<ul>
<li> <code>link</code>: link function used

</li>
<li> <code>prevalence</code>: proportion of y = 1

</li>
<li> <code>h2_liability</code>: h2 on liability scale

</li>
<li> <code>h2_observed</code>: h2 on observed (0/1) scale
via Dempster-Falconer transformation

</li>
<li> <code>auc</code>: Area Under ROC Curve (Wilcoxon-MWW)

</li>
<li> <code>fitted</code>: fitted probabilities P(y = 1)

</li>
<li> <code>converged</code>: always TRUE for single-step

</li></ul>



### References

VanRaden (2008) Efficient methods to compute genomic predictions.
<em>J. Dairy Sci.</em> 91:4414-4423.

Da (2015) Multi-allelic haplotype model for genomic prediction.
<em>BMC Genet.</em> 16:144.

Dempster &amp; Falconer (1950) Interpretation of high and low liability.
<em>Ann. Hum. Genet.</em> 31:195-203.

Johnson &amp; Thompson (1995) Restricted maximum likelihood estimation
of variance components. <em>J. Dairy Sci.</em> 78:449-456.

### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masreml")

d        <- load_data("small")
y        <- d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_snp;  names(y) <- d$pheno$id
y_binary <- as.integer(d$pheno$y_bin_qtl_snp); names(y_binary) <- d$pheno$id

# ── Continuous trait ─────────────────────────────────────
# SNP additive GBLUP (markers list, masreml builds G internally)
fit <- masreml(y = y, markers = list(snp_add = d$snp))
summary(fit)

# multi-allelic additive only (d$mh is auto-detected as a hap-block matrix)
fit <- masreml(y = y, markers = list(mh_add = d$mh))

# Combined SNP additive + dominance
fit <- masreml(
  y       = y,
  markers = list(snp_add = d$snp, snp_dom = d$snp),
  method  = "AI"
)

# Pre-built G matrix
G   <- build_G_snp(d$snp)
fit <- masreml(y = y, G = list(snp_add = G))

# ── Binary trait ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Binary GBLUP (logit link, default HE)
fit <- masreml(y = y_binary, markers = list(snp_add = d$snp),
               trait = "binary")
summary(fit)

# Binary with probit link
fit <- masreml(y = y_binary, markers = list(snp_add = d$snp),
               trait = "binary", link = "probit")




```
